answer: Identity slots are capped by the handful of abutment sockets under the only canyon bridge that can carry a bonded trunk. Each socket holds one mature juniper, whose unique resin chromatogram and ring map are published. Auditors re-core the tree, compare those marks to the registry, and require the bound key to sign a nonce whose timestamp is checked against the observatory's nebula clock. Two keys claiming one socket void the deposit. An attacker who wants a hundred fake agents must buy, plant, and pass assay on a hundred scarce abutment trees, paying full cost for every extra identity.
